tasks.title: Accept-time gate: wire the classifiers into _auto_commit_accepted (Layer 1)
acceptance_criteria: orchestrator exposes _integration_smoke_gate_enabled(state_dir) -> bool and _run_integration_smoke_gate(task, files_touched, state_dir, task_id, staging_path, worktree_root, result, working_dir) -> bool, both invoked inside _auto_commit_accepted immediately after the wire-up block.

when integration_smoke_gate is enabled, _run_integration_smoke_gate is called to classify touched modules using is_io_bound, and rejects any I/O-bound module lacking an executing integration oracle via _rollback_rejected_commit, git_integration.remove_staging_worktree, _mark_blocked(outcome='missing_integration_smoke'), writing to impl_progress.jsonl, and returning False.
when the flag is OFF, the gate is a strict no-op and does not alter the accept/merge behavior.
tests/harness/test_integration_smoke_accept_gate.py passes as an edge-asserting oracle asserting block/merge conditions end-to-end.

spec.objective: Add the load-bearing accept-time gate to harness/orchestrator.py, mirroring the wire-up gate line-for-line, to reject commits touching I/O-bound modules that lack an executing integration oracle, gated by the autowork.integration_smoke_gate flag.
functional_requirements: Add _integration_smoke_gate_enabled(state_dir) -> bool that loads config via load_config() and returns config.get('autowork', {}).get('integration_smoke_gate', False). Fail-safe to False on exceptions.
Add _run_integration_smoke_gate(task, files_touched, state_dir, task_id, staging_path, worktree_root, result, working_dir) -> bool that returns True to reject and False to proceed.
In _run_integration_smoke_gate, identify touched python modules (files_touched ending in .py not under tests/).
Read each touched module's source from staging_path and classify it using is_io_bound from harness.integration_smoke.
For every I/O-bound module, extract committed test sources in files_touched (ending in .py under tests/) and read their content from staging_path.

Verify the test set with has_executing_integration_oracle. If any I/O-bound module has no executing integration oracle, reject using _rollback_rejected_commit, removing the staging worktree, marking task blocked as missing_integration_smoke, appending to impl_progress.jsonl, and returning True.
Call the helpers in _auto_commit_accepted immediately after the wire-up gate block: if _integration_smoke_gate_enabled(state_dir): if _run_integration_smoke_gate(...): return False
spec.interfaces: Exposes _integration_smoke_gate_enabled(state_dir) -> bool and _run_integration_smoke_gate(task, files_touched, state_dir, task_id, staging_path, worktree_root, result, working_dir) -> bool from harness/orchestrator.py.
edge_cases: Pure-logic touched module (non-I/O-bound) -> does not require integration oracle, merged successfully.
I/O-bound touched module with executing integration oracle -> passes checks, merged successfully.
I/O-bound touched module without executing integration oracle -> rejected, rollback triggered, returns False.
Integration smoke gate flag is OFF -> gate is bypassed, normal accept/merge behavior.
non_goals: Do NOT create any new production files in this leaf; import classifiers from harness.integration_smoke.
Do NOT alter the wire-up gate or any current behavior or passing tests.
Do NOT spawn agents, make network/model/API calls, or add un-injected subprocesses.
Do NOT flip the autowork.integration_smoke_gate flag to True; it must default to False.
spec.implementation_notes: Mirror the structure of wire_up_gate line-for-line. Import classifiers dynamically inside the gate function to avoid startup crashes if harness.integration_smoke does not exist yet. Use _rollback_rejected_commit, git_integration.remove_staging_worktree, and write_jsonl_row for rollbacks.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Temp git repositories and staging worktrees setup by pytest fixtures.

token_budget_ratio.note: Implementation is straightforward wiring, while test verification requires complex edge-asserting setup over a mock git repository.
